deep_analysis.executive_intro:
Across 248 FTSE names, the screen is cautious overall: 144 holds (58%) and 42 avoids (17%) outweigh 17 strong buys (7%) and 45 buys (18%). The five highest-ranked names are all labeled strong buy on the raw scorecard but were downgraded to buy after FCF and dividend overlays—so “cheap on multiples” is common, while cash-flow reconciliation is not. Sector clustering is visible among the leaders: three Industrials (FGP.L, MEGP.L, MGNS.L), plus Communication Services (ITV.L) and Healthcare (HIK.L). Industrials is also the largest bucket in the full universe (50 names), so a portfolio built from this list would tilt cyclical and operational rather than financials-heavy. Treat headline yields and FCF-yield passes skeptically: filing, screen TTM (often unverified), and company-adjusted FCF frequently diverge, and several names show statutory vs management dividend coverage gaps the models flag but do not fully resolve.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Industrials, composite 85%, 14/22 models, all five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), conviction 73% (persistent, 17 weeks). Quantitative appeal is classic value: P/E 8.6, P/B 1.3, yield 4.2%, ROE 16.7%, screening D/E 19%, with passes including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG, Neff PEGY, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), and Earnings Quality. Failures include FCF Yield (canonical FCF basis diverges from filing), Economic Moat (ROE/margins below moat thresholds), and Financial Health (weak liquidity). The action note highlights FCF basis mismatch (filing £362.6M vs screen TTM £302.8M vs company-adj £73.8M) and a leverage override (Yahoo D/E 161% vs £137.7m adj. net debt on filing). With two other Industrials in the top five, sector concentration is material. **Verdict: watchlist** — strong multi-model cheapness and Piotroski support, but reconciled FCF and liquidity failures argue for proof on cash before sizing up.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Industrials, composite 82%, 15/22 models, five families, conviction 72%. Metrics are aggressive value: P/E 8.0, P/B 2.3, yield 6.8%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%, with passes including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, and Neff PEGY. Lynch PEG and Piotroski (6/9) fail, as does Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion). Overlays flag an interim dividend cut, interim-quality issues (interim EPS decline ~3.9%, net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× vs gross 1.68×), earnings growth basis divergence (>300 bps: statutory 4.5% vs filing core 0.4%), and FCF basis mismatch (filing £25.2M vs screen TTM £15.6M). Third Industrials name in the set adds cluster risk. **Verdict: pass** — headline yield and ROE look compelling, but dividend cut, sub-1× net coverage, and growth/cash-quality warnings dominate the adjusted buy signal.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Communication Services, composite 81%, 15/22 models, five families, but conviction only 51% (downgraded). Key metrics: P/E 11.7, P/B 1.5, yield 7.1%, ROE 13.5%; passes include Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, and Lynch PEG. Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, and Piotroski (3/9) fail. Timing is “accumulate” (RSI 41, below 200-day MA, downtrend), with overlays for dividend sustainability (statutory cover ≤1.05× with weak Piotroski), FCF three-way mismatch (>15% across bases), and profit-to-cash 65% vs 83% (−18pp YoY). FCF filing £148M vs screen TTM £211.9M vs company-adj £187M; statutory vs management dividend coverage 0.79× vs 1.53×. **Verdict: watchlist** — favourable entry timing and deep value screens, but the lowest conviction in the group and weak quality/cash trends warrant confirmation before accumulation.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Healthcare, composite 78%, 12/22 models (fewest in the top five), five families, conviction 70%. P/E 11.9, P/B 1.8, yield 4.2%, ROE 15.4%; passes include Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, and Quality Value. FCF Yield fails (3.7% below 5%), Lynch PEG fails on low growth, Economic Moat and Piotroski (6/9) fail, and Earnings Quality fails on weak free-cash conversion. FCF basis mismatch is extreme in the JSON: filing $119M vs screen TTM (unverified) $14.4M; statutory vs management dividend coverage 0.64× vs 1.31×. **Verdict: watchlist** — reasonable pharmaceutical multiples and quality-value passes, but unverified TTM FCF and sub-1× net dividend coverage block a confident accumulate call.

**MGNS.L (Morgan Sindall Group plc)** — Industrials, composite 81%, 16/22 models (most in group), five families, conviction 69%. P/E 10.4, P/B 2.4, yield 4.0%, ROE 26.1%, D/E 18%; passes include Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG, and Piotroski (8/9). Failures are mostly “not deep enough” (Graham Defensive, Net-Net, Schloss, Deep Value) plus Economic Moat on ROA/margins. FCF basis overlay notes filing £170.7M vs screen TTM £141.5M; net FCF dividend coverage ~2.59×. RSI 31 with price below 50- and 200-day MAs (downtrend) but neutral timing label. **Verdict: accumulate** — strongest model breadth and cash/dividend metrics in the top five, with overlays lighter than peers, accepting Industrials cyclicality and construction exposure as the main portfolio-level caveat.

- FGP.L: UK bus/rail contract and regulatory pricing risk not in the screen; pension and long-dated transport obligations are an open question from this JSON alone.
- FGP.L: Yahoo vs filing leverage (161% vs £137.7m adj. net debt, IFRS lease gross-up) — governance and disclosure consistency around debt/leases need manual review.
- MEGP.L: Photo-booth/vending-style capital intensity and location economics — cyclical consumer/travel exposure not flagged (`cyclical_exposure_detected`: false) but qualitatively relevant.
- MEGP.L: Interim dividend cut with high trailing yield pass — board capital-allocation intent and payout policy are unresolved.
- ITV.L: Structural advertising/streaming competition and content spend cycles — screen shows weak Piotroski and moat fails but not franchise erosion or regulatory (Ofcom/public-service) shifts.
- ITV.L: Balance-sheet/leverage called out in Schloss/Economic Moat failures (“too much leverage”) without pension detail in JSON — pension deficit status is an open question.
- HIK.L: US/generic pharma pricing, FDA/regulatory, and pipeline litigation risk absent from value metrics; screen only hints via earnings quality and FCF noise.
- HIK.L: Emerging-market and currency mix (USD filing FCF vs London listing) — governance and related-party risk not assessable from this payload.
- MGNS.L: UK construction and public-sector project cyclicality — screen does not model order-book concentration or contract loss on mega-projects.
- MGNS.L: Acquisition/integration and working-capital swings typical of construction groups — not captured despite strong ROE and Piotroski pass.
deep_analysis.red_flags:
NAMES WORTH DEEPER RESEARCH

- ITV.L — Which FCF definition (filing £148M, company-adj £187M, or screen TTM £211.9M) supports a 7.1% yield, and is the dividend sustainable on statutory OCF−CapEx cover (~1.0×)?
- FGP.L — Why do company-adjusted FCF (£73.8M) and filing FCF (£362.6M) diverge so sharply, and does adjusted net debt (£137.7m) fully reflect lease and contract liabilities?
- MEGP.L — Was the interim dividend cut a one-off rebasing or a signal of structural cash pressure given net FCF/dividend coverage of 0.84× and filing core EPS growth of 0.4%?

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run screened 248 names with a cautious distribution (144 hold, 42 avoid vs 17 strong buy and 45 buy). The five highest raw scorecard names were all strong buy but were downgraded to buy after FCF and dividend overlays, so headline cheapness is common while cash-flow and payout reconciliation is not. Buy-tier memo snapshots for the sampled FTSE names are uniformly “strong” with accumulate verdicts and deep filing counts (no entries in `thin_filing_tickers`), yet deep-analysis narrative flags three-way FCF mismatches, dividend-cut/coverage issues (e.g. MEGP.L, ITV.L), and leverage/liquidity gaps (e.g. FGP.L)—so conviction on top picks is partially blocked by scoring/overlay and ingest interpretation gaps, not by missing memo files on this FTSE sample. Cross-market ops show `executed`: 29 and full memo throughput while `system_gaps` still flags thin or zero-body memos counted as coverage in euro_depth and filing-ready but not learning_ready sp500 clocks. `so_what_closure` recorded zero new auto-queue, human_gate, or open engineering tasks this snapshot, so FCF enforcement batch work is not newly queued from this closure pass.
post_run_review.persistent_weaknesses:
- **Ingest — RNS/filing bodies (backlog-heavy):** Recurring theme to fetch Investegate/LSE direct HTML/PDF instead of Google News wrappers and to backfill bodies when index shows `with_body: 0` (e.g. AEP.L sample: 31 indexed with zero bodies; MEGP.L: 52 indexed, 0 bodies in backlog sample). rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
